title: Interface lemma is_zero_iff_epi_and_is_iso turns Ext-vanishing into epi + is_iso (Liquid Tensor Theorem 1.1)
intent: Reduce the main theorem of the Liquid Tensor Experiment — Ext^i(ℳ_{p'} S, V) ≅ 0 for all i > 0 — to two separate facts by applying the interface lemma is_zero_iff_epi_and_is_iso to the short exact sequence laurent_measures.short_exact: the Ext-vanishing goal becomes 'epi at 0 and is_iso above 0', which laurent_measures.epi_and_is_iso supplies exactly, leaving only its T-inv hypothesis to discharge.

lemma is_zero_iff_epi_and_is_iso
  {A₁ A₂ A₃ : C} (f : A₁ ⟶ A₂) (g : A₂ ⟶ A₃) (B : C) (h : short_exact f g) :
  (∀ i > 0, is_zero (((Ext' i).obj (op A₃)).obj B)) ↔
  (epi (((Ext' 0).map f.op).app B) ∧ ∀ i > 0, is_iso (((Ext' i).map f.op).app B)) :=

applicability.goal_shape: A goal '∀ i > 0, Ext i A B ≅ 0' (Ext-vanishing), where Ext is defined through the derived category Ext' and the goal mentions a known short exact sequence f, g with A = the right object. The interface lemma rewrites the vanishing statement into 'epi of the Ext' 0-map ∧ is_iso of every positive Ext' i-map', i.e. it stops unfolding Ext' and works with epi/is_iso of the induced maps instead.
applicability.use_when: the goal is an Ext-vanishing (or any 'all terms of a cohomology theory vanish') statement for which you already have (or can prove) a short exact sequence, and a separate argument proves the epi + is_iso form; the interface lemma is a reusable iff, so it pays for itself the second time it is applied.
applicability.avoid_when: no short exact sequence is available to supply the h : short_exact f g argument; the epi/is_iso form is no easier than the original vanishing (e.g. when you would prove it by the same five-term chase anyway); or the Ext-vanishing is the final object of study rather than a stepping stone to a concrete epi/is_iso fact.

consequences: The interface lemma shifts the goal from a quantified Ext-vanishing to an epi/is_iso statement, so the main proof must supply a short exact sequence (short_exact) and a lemma that proves the epi/is_iso form (epi_and_is_iso), plus any hypotheses that lemma needs (here hV : T.inv v = 2 • v, discharged by two lines of rewriting). The interface lemma only holds for i > 0, so the i = 0 term is split out as 'epi', not 'is_iso' — a client must not forget that the 0-th map is only epi. Because epi_and_is_iso itself reuses the same interface lemma on a different short exact sequence (invpoly.short_exact), the three children are not independent: changing the interface lemma changes both the glue and the epi_and_is_iso child.
